question: Why should you be extra careful using thermal compresses on patients with diabetic neuropathy?

options.A: It automatically causes severe allergic reactions to moisture
options.B: It prevents the compress material from sticking to the skin surface
options.C: It speeds up blood sugar absorption into local muscles dangerously
options.D: Patients cannot accurately feel temperature extremes to warn of tissue damage

explanation: When nerve sensation is damaged, patients might not feel if the compress is burning them until real injury has already happened. Safety first! [learn more](GNS221_U3_T9#GNS221_U3_T9_h4)

question: Why is it so effective to partner with traditional and religious leaders when promoting reproductive health?

options.A: They distribute free contraceptives directly to hospitals
options.B: They are licensed medical doctors trained in midwifery
options.C: They hold significant influence over community beliefs and health practices
options.D: They manage the national budget for health infrastructure

explanation: Local leaders are deeply respected by the community. When they support health initiatives, community members are much more likely to listen and adopt healthy practices. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T4#GNS216_U1_T4_h6)

question: Why are hospitals often shielded from vicarious liability when dealing with true independent contractors?

options.A: The hospital does not direct or control the daily details of their work
options.B: Independent contractors are forbidden by law from making clinical errors
options.C: Staffing agencies pay a special tax that waives all hospital legal claims
options.D: Independent contractors do not possess valid nursing license certificates

explanation: If a worker is truly independent and manages their own methods, the classic boss-worker control link isn't there, protecting the facility. [learn more](GST321_U10_T6#GST321_U10_T6_h5)

question: What role does regular feedback play in the philosophy of MBO?

options.A: It replaces the need for any further clinical training sessions
options.B: It allows upper management to change rules without notice
options.C: It serves as formal documentation for immediate disciplinary action
options.D: It helps staff track their progress and adjust actions early

explanation: Continuous feedback gives workers the chance to correct course before performance targets are missed entirely. [learn more](GST321_U2_T5#GST321_U2_T5_h2)

question: A discharged patient with a spinal injury cannot afford their wheelchair or follow-up therapy. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Buy the expensive equipment with personal salary
options.B: Tell them to stop all medications immediately
options.C: Say financial issues are none of nursing's business
options.D: Refer the patient to medical social services for financial counseling and support

explanation: You don't have to pay out of your own pocket! Connecting the patient to the medical social work department is the right professional step to bridge that gap. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T12#GNS225_U5_T12_h7)

question: Why should nurses treat every pregnancy as though complications could happen?

options.A: Routine delivery is considered a surgical emergency
options.B: Standard tests are rarely accurate during gestation
options.C: Complications can occur suddenly without prior warning
options.D: Most pregnant women develop chronic illnesses

explanation: Exactly! Even a smooth pregnancy can change quickly, so staying alert helps us catch issues early and save lives. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h1)

question: Why is keeping a food diary helpful for someone with gas issues?

options.A: It completely cures lactose intolerance without any medication.
options.B: It measures the exact volume of gas produced each hour.
options.C: It helps the patient and nurse pinpoint specific foods that trigger excess gas.
options.D: It guarantees the patient will lose weight within the first week.

explanation: Writing down meals and symptoms helps connect the dots so patients can figure out which foods don't agree with them. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T10#GNS212_U1_T10_h7)

question: Where does most of the money for public healthcare come from?

options.A: Donations from international pharmaceutical manufacturing corporations
options.B: Profits generated exclusively by private for-profit clinics
options.C: Direct out-of-pocket payments made by emergency room patients
options.D: Government revenue and taxation derived from national economic output

explanation: Public healthcare is funded mostly through taxes and government revenue. When the economy generates wealth, public services get their share. [learn more](GST322_U3_T6#GST322_U3_T6_h5)

question: Which heart chamber is responsible for pumping freshly oxygenated blood out to the rest of the newborn's body?

options.A: Right atrium
options.B: Left ventricle
options.C: Left atrium
options.D: Right ventricle

explanation: The left ventricle receives oxygenated blood from the lungs and pumps it into the aorta to supply the systemic circulation. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h6)

question: Which of these is most likely to make a community reject an IEC material?

options.A: It is handed out by a registered community health nurse.
options.B: It contains too many pictures and too little heavy medical jargon.
options.C: It is printed using black ink instead of colorful ink.
options.D: It violates local social norms or triggers cultural taboos.

explanation: Even if your medical facts are 100% correct, a community will quickly turn away from materials that clash with their cultural values or taboos. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T6#GNS124_U5_T6_h2)

question: What does the term 'phenomenology' mean in psychiatric nursing?

options.A: The genetic mapping of hereditary psychiatric traits
options.B: The physical lab tests used to check blood chemistry
options.C: The subjective, lived experience of the patient's symptoms
options.D: The mathematical chance of making a full recovery

explanation: Phenomenology is all about stepping into the patient's shoes to understand what their illness actually feels like from their own unique point of view. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T1#GNS314_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why is protecting patient privacy so important during a chart review for a study?

options.A: Hospital computers will delete files if names are left visible
options.B: Researchers gather sensitive personal and clinical data from multiple records
options.C: Patients must sign a new consent form every single day
options.D: Statistical software requires patient names to calculate numbers

explanation: Spot on! Medical records hold very private information, so keeping patient data strictly confidential is a top priority for nurses and researchers. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T12#GNS224_U1_T12_h4)

question: Why can relying too much on assistive technology become a problem in patient care?

options.A: It can reduce human interaction and lead to patient isolation
options.B: It automatically cures all chronic illnesses within days
options.C: It forces patients to perform rigorous physical exercises
options.D: It eliminates the need for any future medical research

explanation: You're doing great! While tech is helpful, leaning on machines too much can cut down on the warm, meaningful human contact patients need. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T4#GNS113_U4_T4_h6)

question: In the diathesis-stress model, what does 'diathesis' refer to?

options.A: An underlying vulnerability or predisposition
options.B: The chemical name for antipsychotic drugs
options.C: A sudden environmental crisis or life event
options.D: A physical test used to measure brainwaves

explanation: Diathesis represents the biological or psychological vulnerability a person carries before a major stressor triggers an illness. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T4#GNS314_U2_T4_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common unhealthy coping mechanism associated with high chronic stress?

options.A: Engaging in regular physical activity
options.B: Turning to tobacco use or excessive smoking
options.C: Adopting poor dietary habits and overeating
options.D: Withdrawing from social and physical movement

explanation: Regular physical exercise is a healthy stress management tool, whereas smoking, poor diet, and physical withdrawal are unhealthy responses to stress. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h7)

question: What is the most effective nursing action when supporting stressed parents of a newly diagnosed child?

options.A: Focus only on the child and ignore parental emotional health
options.B: Tell them to stop worrying because children always outgrow it
options.C: Connect them with local parent support groups and active listening
options.D: Advise them to change schools immediately without investigation

explanation: Emotional support and peer connections help parents cope with the challenges of navigating a new diagnosis. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h7)

question: What is the main benefit of using a team-based structure in a workplace?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any managers or supervisors
options.B: It prevents employees from ever collaborating with outsiders
options.C: It ensures strict top-down centralized control over decisions
options.D: It breaks down departmental barriers and empowers staff

explanation: Team-based designs get people working together across different departments so everyone feels empowered to share ideas and get things done. [learn more](GST321_U1_T10#GST321_U1_T10_h4)

question: A nurse in a busy Lagos clinic wants to cut down patient waiting times without buying new computers. What is the best approach?

options.A: Complain to the patients about the lack of staff instead of changing anything
options.B: Refuse to see any patients who arrive after eight o'clock in the morning
options.C: Use a PDSA cycle to test reorganizing the patient triage and record-pulling process
options.D: Wait until the government donates brand new digital tablets to the clinic

explanation: You nailed it! Reorganizing how we do things using a quick PDSA test is a fantastic way to improve patient flow without spending money. [learn more](GST319_U3_T5#GST319_U3_T5_h7)

question: What kind of survey question gives people a fixed list of choices to pick from?

options.A: Unstructured item
options.B: Open-ended item
options.C: Closed-ended item
options.D: Narrative item

explanation: Closed-ended items restrict answers to predefined options, which makes counting and analyzing the responses much easier for your research project. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h2)

question: Why do food workers in Nigeria need a mandatory medical certificate?

options.A: To prove they are free from infectious diseases before handling food
options.B: To test how well they can cook local dishes
options.C: To help local government offices generate revenue
options.D: To figure out the right salary level for kitchen staff

explanation: Medical checks ensure that kitchen staff aren't carrying hidden infections that could easily spread to the meals they prepare. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h7)

question: What happens to a blood pressure reading if the cuff used on the patient's arm is too small?

options.A: It remains completely normal
options.B: It reads falsely high
options.C: It reads falsely low
options.D: It drops to zero

explanation: A cuff that is too small requires more pressure to compress the artery, resulting in an artificially elevated reading. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T16#GNS324_U4_T16_h3)

question: How do benzimidazole medications primarily get rid of parasitic worms in the gut?

options.A: By increasing calcium levels to cause permanent muscle spasm
options.B: By blocking glucose uptake and depleting energy stores
options.C: By binding directly to bacterial cell walls in the gut
options.D: By dissolving the outer protective skin of the worm

explanation: Think of it as cutting off the worm's food supply! Benzimidazoles stop the parasite from absorbing glucose, so it runs out of energy and dies. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h2)

question: Why must sexual partners be treated at the same time for a sexually transmitted infection?

options.A: To eliminate the need for follow-up blood tests altogether
options.B: To prevent passing the infection back and forth between partners
options.C: To speed up the manufacturing process of the antibiotic drugs
options.D: To ensure the laboratory costs remain low for the clinic

explanation: Spot on! Treating both partners simultaneously stops the ping-pong effect of reinfecting each other. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T12#GNS312_U3_T12_h4)

question: How does overall energy balance affect a patient's body weight over time?

options.A: Consuming more calories than expended results in weight gain
options.B: BMR increases infinitely whenever extra food is eaten
options.C: Weight changes only occur if fluid balance is disturbed
options.D: Exercise alone determines weight without regard to food intake

explanation: Energy balance dictates that excess consumed calories are stored by the body, leading to weight gain. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T015#GNS227_U2_T015_h5)

question: What is the best way for a nurse to find out if a patient is trying a risky diet?

options.A: Scolding the patient immediately for reading health advice online
options.B: Asking open-ended questions about how the patient manages their weight
options.C: Threatening to report the use of herbal supplements to the hospital board
options.D: Refusing to provide medical care until the patient stops buying vitamins

explanation: Patients won't open up if you judge them. Friendly, open-ended questions make them feel safe to tell the truth. You're going to be a great nurse! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T018#GNS227_U2_T018_h6)

question: A patient is admitted with severe heart failure and fluid accumulation in the lungs. Why is a low salt diet ordered?

options.A: To prevent further fluid retention and reduce cardiac workload
options.B: To improve digestion and absorption of oral medications
options.C: To stimulate red blood cell production in the bone marrow
options.D: To cure the underlying viral infection in the heart muscle

explanation: Restricting salt stops the body from holding onto extra water, which lessens the volume of blood the weakened heart has to pump. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h3)

question: Why do we need a team of different professionals in palliative care?

options.A: Hospital regulations require at least ten staff members per patient.
options.B: No single profession can address all physical, emotional, and spiritual needs.
options.C: Nurses only handle administrative paperwork in palliative settings.
options.D: Doctors are not allowed to talk to family members directly.

explanation: No single person knows it all! Caring for someone with a serious illness takes doctors, nurses, social workers, and spiritual leaders all working hand-in-hand to cover every angle. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h4)

question: How does the growing uterus help cause vulval varicosities?

options.A: It directly damages the external skin of the labia
options.B: It blocks the arterial supply to the perineum
options.C: It releases enzymes that weaken capillary membranes
options.D: It presses on pelvic veins and slows down blood return

explanation: As the baby and uterus grow heavier, they act like a heavy blanket pressing down on the big pelvic veins. This slows down the blood trying to flow back up, causing it to pool below. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T9#GNS216_U5_T9_h2)

question: What is the recommended compression rate per minute for adult CPR?

options.A: 60 to 80 compressions per minute
options.B: 140 to 160 compressions per minute
options.C: 100 to 120 compressions per minute
options.D: 40 to 50 compressions per minute

explanation: Aim for a steady, brisk rhythm of 100 to 120 compressions per minute. Fun fact: pumping to the beat of the song 'Stayin' Alive' helps hit this exact speed! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T6#GNS321_U2_T6_h3)

question: What is a baby or young child's biggest emotional need?

options.A: Having their own money from an early age
options.B: Being left alone to learn how to be independent early
options.C: Advanced problem-solving skills for handling stress
options.D: Consistent love and predictable routines to build trust

explanation: Little ones thrive on safety. Predictable routines and steady affection from caregivers give them the secure foundation they need to grow. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T6#GNS314_U1_T6_h3)

question: Why must a patient with liver cirrhosis watch their daily sodium intake?

options.A: To prevent fluid from pooling in the abdominal cavity
options.B: To prevent painful muscle cramps in the legs
options.C: To encourage rapid absorption of dietary iron
options.D: To stop sudden spikes in blood glucose levels

explanation: Spot on! Liver issues can cause fluid to collect in the belly (ascites), and eating too much salt makes this swelling much worse. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T008#GNS227_U6_T008_h3)

question: Why should a nurse manager care about keeping the ward staff motivated?

options.A: It allows the manager to reduce overall nursing salaries
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for hospital policies
options.C: It leads to safer patient care and better staff retention
options.D: It guarantees that nurses will never make charting errors

explanation: You got it! When nurses feel valued and motivated, patients get safer care, and people are much happier staying on the team. [learn more](GST321_U3_T5#GST321_U3_T5_h1)

question: What is the main responsibility of the WHO during a global health emergency?

options.A: Deploying military forces to enforce quarantines globally
options.B: Managing the financial budgets of all local hospitals in a disaster zone
options.C: Building permanent housing infrastructure for displaced persons
options.D: Providing technical guidance and coordinating the global health response

explanation: You nailed it! The WHO leads the medical side of things—setting health standards, tracking illnesses, and guiding doctors and nurses. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T10#GNS315_U1_T10_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of a downward referral in mental health?

options.A: To clear hospital beds by discharging clients without any follow-up plan
options.B: To transfer chronic cases to out-of-state traditional healing homes
options.C: To return stabilized clients to community clinics for ongoing maintenance care
options.D: To punish clients who refuse to take part in group therapy sessions

explanation: Downward referral steps patients down to community care once they are stable, freeing up specialist beds while keeping them supported close to home. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h4)

question: What is the gold-standard laboratory test used to confirm an Ebola infection?

options.A: Routine microscopic examination of red blood cells
options.B: X-ray imaging of the chest
options.C: Stool microscopy for parasites
options.D: Reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR)

explanation: Correct! RT-PCR is the reliable test that catches the virus's RNA in blood samples. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T11#GNS214_U1_T11_h4)

question: What was the core belief of the Moral Treatment movement?

options.A: Mental illness should be met with kindness and a peaceful environment
options.B: Patients must be permanently separated from society
options.C: Strict physical punishment is necessary to cure madness
options.D: Spiritual exorcisms are the only true cure for mental disorders

explanation: Moral treatment shifted care away from cruelty and towards dignity, fresh air, useful work, and compassionate human interaction. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T3#GNS314_U1_T3_h3)

question: What happens to the foetal skull bones during the process of molding?

options.A: They compress tightly and overlap each other
options.B: They dissolve temporarily under pelvic pressure
options.C: They expand outward to make the head rounder
options.D: They fracture completely to ease delivery

explanation: Molding is the natural overlapping of un-fused cranial bones to help the head adjust to the shape of the birth canal. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T16#GNS121_U6_T16_h1)

question: What is a major hurdle when introducing telehealth gadgets to home care patients?

options.A: Internet access is legally banned in residential areas
options.B: Physicians refuse to look at remote monitoring data
options.C: Lack of digital literacy among patients and families
options.D: Telehealth devices completely eliminate all illnesses

explanation: Many patients—especially older adults—might feel intimidated by tablets or apps until you patiently walk them through it step by step. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T3#GNS324_U2_T3_h7)

question: Why is it important to talk about the limitations of your study in the discussion?

options.A: It ensures that other nurses will never attempt a similar study
options.B: It demonstrates professional honesty and acknowledges weaknesses in the design
options.C: It gives the journal editors an excuse to reject the final manuscript
options.D: It proves that the statistical software used was completely flawless

explanation: No study is 100% perfect. Admitting your limitations shows maturity and helps others know how to build on your work. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h7)

question: Which of these best describes 'disenfranchised grief'?

options.A: Loss that society does not openly acknowledge or validate
options.B: Grief caused exclusively by the loss of a physical body part
options.C: Sudden grief that disappears within a few hours of the event
options.D: Mourning that only occurs after a legal dispute over an estate

explanation: Well done! Disenfranchised grief happens when society doesn't give someone space or recognition to mourn openly. Think of it as a hidden or unsupported loss. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T5#GNS221_U4_T5_h2)

question: Why do infection control teams need members from many different hospital departments?

options.A: Because infection prevention touches every area of patient care and facility operations
options.B: Because cleaning staff are the only ones trained to use chemical disinfectants
options.C: Because labor laws require equal representation from all hospital departments
options.D: Because doctors alone cannot write prescriptions for powerful antibiotics

explanation: Exactly! Stopping germs takes teamwork—from clinicians and lab scientists to admin staff—because infection risks can pop up anywhere. [learn more](GST114_U2_T22#GST114_U2_T22_h2)

question: A clinic nurse notices frequent shortages of basic drugs and sutures. What is a major reason for this in many African nations?

options.A: International agencies ban the importation of basic surgical items
options.B: Nurses generally mismanage the medical supplies in hospital warehouses
options.C: Patients refuse to accept free medications from the government
options.D: National health budgets frequently fall short of the Abuja Declaration target

explanation: When budgets fall short of targets like the Abuja 15%, clinics struggle to buy everyday essentials like gloves, drugs, and suture materials. [learn more](GST322_U3_T2#GST322_U3_T2_h3)

question: You notice a patient has dry, brittle hair, pale skin, and spoon-shaped nails. What part of the nutritional assessment is this?

options.A: Dietary history recall
options.B: Clinical observations
options.C: Biochemical tests
options.D: Anthropometric tracking

explanation: When you look directly at the patient's body for physical signs of nutrition issues, you are doing a clinical observation! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T014#GNS227_U4_T014_h3)

question: Why should nurses teach patients to avoid unprescribed supplements when taking synergistic drugs?

options.A: Additional substances could trigger unpredictable and dangerous interactions
options.B: Supplements always neutralize the healing properties of prescription drugs
options.C: Supplements make laboratory blood draws completely inaccurate
options.D: Over-the-counter products are illegal to take alongside antibiotics

explanation: Over-the-counter herbs and supplements can mess with drug processing in the body, leading to accidental overdoses or weird reactions. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T6#GNS125_U5_T6_h7)

question: Which condition often brings a patient to a subacute care unit?

options.A: Active cardiac arrest requiring immediate chest compressions
options.B: Routine annual physical examination and blood tests
options.C: Undiagnosed chronic fatigue without any physical findings
options.D: Recovery following a total knee replacement surgery

explanation: Correct! Post-surgical recovery that needs intensive physical therapy is a classic reason for subacute admission. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T8#GNS324_U5_T8_h2)

question: What is the main hazard of leaving heavy oxygen cylinders unmounted inside an ambulance?

options.A: They make the ambulance engine consume more diesel fuel
options.B: They will automatically run out of medical oxygen faster
options.C: They can become dangerous projectiles during sudden braking
options.D: They interfere with the vehicle's internal electrical system

explanation: Sudden stops create massive forward momentum, turning loose heavy items into severe safety hazards for the crew and patient. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T9#GNS315_U3_T9_h2)

question: Which finding is considered a vital part of assessing a patient with a suspected emerging infection?

options.A: Evaluating the patient's current employment income level
options.B: Checking the patient's past childhood immunization cards
options.C: Measuring the patient's daily fluid intake at home
options.D: A detailed travel and recent exposure history

explanation: Knowing where a patient has traveled and who they have been in contact with is essential for identifying rare or outbreak-related pathogens. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h5)

question: Why do we involve family members so closely in Community-Based Rehabilitation?

options.A: Families provide continuous daily support and reinforce therapy goals
options.B: Families are legally required to pay for all hospital equipment
options.C: Nurses prefer to avoid visiting patients at home
options.D: Community members lack basic literacy skills

explanation: Since care continues outside the hospital, family members are your greatest allies in making sure the patient keeps up with their daily exercises and routines. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T17#GNS225_U5_T17_h2)

question: If an expectant mother reports a sudden decrease in fetal movement, what should you suspect first?

options.A: The fetus has dropped into the pelvic cavity
options.B: The mother is simply too busy to notice kicks
options.C: Normal sleeping patterns of a full-term baby
options.D: Potential fetal distress or oxygen deprivation

explanation: Always take a drop in baby kicks seriously! It can be a vital warning sign that the baby is under distress and needs an urgent check-up. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T49#GNS214_U1_T49_h5)

question: During which step of mobilisation do community members and nurses figure out what resources and tasks are needed?

options.A: Immediate closure
options.B: Final evaluation
options.C: Strict policing
options.D: Action planning

explanation: Action planning is where the community maps out tasks, responsibilities, and timelines using local resources. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T1#GNS124_U4_T1_h5)

question: Which of the following is a primary objective of community mobilisation?

options.A: Closing down local primary health centers
options.B: Reducing the number of working nurses
options.C: Empowering local populations to demand better services
options.D: Increasing government taxes for medical supplies

explanation: Empowerment helps community members gain the confidence and voice needed to advocate for their own health rights. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h2)

question: A patient asks how to view their recent laboratory test results from home. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Guide the patient on how to access their secure online health portal
options.B: Print the entire hospital database and mail it to their home
options.C: Tell the patient that viewing lab results is strictly illegal for laypeople
options.D: Read all hospital lab results out loud over a public phone call

explanation: Nurses empower patients by showing them how to use secure patient portals to check their own health records. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h6)

question: When reviewing literature, what do we call the missing or weakly studied areas in current research?

options.A: Financial grants
options.B: Research gaps
options.C: Patient registries
options.D: Nursing licenses

explanation: Spotting what is missing in current studies points directly to research gaps that need investigation. Great job thinking like a researcher! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T5#GNS217_U3_T5_h2)

question: When should a nurse collect a wound culture specimen in relation to starting antibiotics?

options.A: At the exact same time as the first dose
options.B: Only after the patient develops a fever
options.C: Before starting the antibiotics
options.D: Three days after finishing the antibiotics

explanation: Always swab or collect cultures *before* giving antibiotics! If you start the drugs first, they'll kill the germs in the sample and you won't find out what's causing the infection. [learn more](GST114_U2_T3#GST114_U2_T3_h9)

question: How do strict professional hierarchies sometimes hurt patient care?

options.A: They discourage junior staff and nurses from sharing critical patient observations
options.B: They ensure that every single medication is administered twice as fast
options.C: They eliminate all forms of communication errors between departments
options.D: They force patients to pay less money for hospital admission fees

explanation: Spot on! When junior staff or nurses feel intimidated by strict ranks, they might hold back life-saving observations out of fear. [learn more](GST321_U7_T3#GST321_U7_T3_h5)

question: In a standard research dataset, what does each row typically represent?

options.A: A summary of missing values
options.B: The final statistical conclusion
options.C: A different measurement scale
options.D: A single participant or subject

explanation: Standard datasets are arranged so that each horizontal row corresponds to one individual participant, while the vertical columns represent the variables measured. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T2#GNS224_U2_T2_h1)

question: When we talk about 'social capital' in a community, what do we mean?

options.A: The trust and supportive networks built through social participation
options.B: The physical infrastructure of roads and water pipes
options.C: The total financial savings kept in local credit unions
options.D: The government grants given to public health clinics

explanation: Great thinking! Social capital is all about the strength of relationships, trust, and neighborly support in a community. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T4#GNS225_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is the most important first step when a nurse needs to assess a patient who has undergone FGM?

options.A: Building trust and providing a safe, private environment
options.B: Performing a physical exam before talking to the patient
options.C: Asking family members to step outside permanently
options.D: Notifying local law enforcement immediately

explanation: You've got it! Because FGM involves deep trauma and shame, you must always build trust and create a safe space before any exam or questioning. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T4#GNS225_U6_T4_h7)

question: What is NOT a recommended way for nurses to handle technology in clinical practice?

options.A: Following hospital data privacy and password protection rules
options.B: Letting computer screens completely replace verbal communication with the patient
options.C: Knowing how to chart manually when the computer system goes down
options.D: Using clinical decision support alerts to verify medication safety

explanation: Technology should support care, not destroy the personal, empathetic connection between the nurse and the patient. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h7)

question: Which group of people should be involved during a community health situation analysis?

options.A: Foreign tourists visiting local tourist attractions
options.B: International pharmaceutical company sales representatives
options.C: Local stakeholders like traditional leaders and women's groups
options.D: Only doctors from the federal capital city

question: What do we call the natural, progressive loss of muscle mass and strength as people grow older?

question: Why did medicine shift from using whole plants to isolating just the active ingredients?

question: How does nursing in the community differ from working in a big hospital ward?

question: How does risk pooling benefit hospitals within the HMO framework?

question: What does it mean when a disease is described as 'endemic' in a community?

question: Which of the following is NOT a safe nursing action after a patient returns from an MRI where they received mild sedation for anxiety?

question: Why are national implementation committees necessary for primary health care?

question: Why must a community health nurse be versatile and take on multiple roles like educator, manager, and clinician?

question: You are about to give an IV antibiotic to your patient. What is the best way to use technology right at that moment?

question: What is a standard check done during a routine antenatal clinic (ANC) visit?

question: What immediate lab test must be done before giving a blood transfusion to a severely anaemic labor patient?

question: Why is simple bed making considered an essential clinical nursing skill rather than just housekeeping?

question: What usually happens when someone skips meals all day and eats one massive meal at night?

question: What is the main goal of the discussion section in a research paper?

question: Which task is a core responsibility of a home health nurse?

question: Which option best describes a holistic psychiatric care plan?

question: Which of the following is NOT a good way to maintain high data quality?

question: What is the main use of Microsoft Word in a healthcare setting?

question: What is the main goal of a two-way referral system in mental health care?

question: What is an example of a direct health injury caused straight away by an earthquake?

question: Why do nurses calculate a patient's BMI during clinical assessments?

question: Why do nursing students need to choose their research topics carefully?

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do right after a needlestick injury?

question: Which of these is NOT an environmental barrier to a nursing student's learning?

question: Why do midwives check both cervical dilation and moulding together on the partograph?

question: What is the primary role of natural anticoagulants like antithrombin III?

options.A: To prevent unwanted clotting in healthy, uninjured blood vessels

options.C: To dissolve large clots that have already formed in the legs
options.D: To speed up the conversion of fibrinogen into solid fibrin

question: Why is it so important for hospitals to ask nurses for their opinion when buying new software?

options.C: Nurses understand the practical bedside workflow and can spot usability issues that affect safety

question: Which specific vitamin needs a special helper protein called 'intrinsic factor' from the stomach to be absorbed properly?

question: A community health nurse working in a rural Nigerian primary health care clinic is struggling to store vaccines properly due to frequent power outages. Which underlying systemic issue does this practical challenge highlight?

question: How often must the injectable contraceptive NET-EN be given to keep working?

question: Why is it important to talk through the exercise steps with your patient beforehand?

question: According to the healthy plate model, how much of your meal should be fruits and non-starchy veggies?

options.A: The entire plate

options.D: Three-quarters

explanation: Half the plate! Packing it with veggies and fruits gives you great fiber and vitamins without overloading on calories. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T003#GNS227_U2_T003_h5)

question: A patient actively moves their arm through space without any nurse assistance. What type of movement is being tested?

options.C: Active range of motion

question: Why is maintaining good hydration especially vital for a bedbound person?

question: A nurse makes a drug dosage mistake and now gets very nervous and avoids preparing intravenous medications. What is this behavior called?

options.C: Professional indifference and apathy
options.D: Hypervigilance and avoidance behavior

question: What do we call a host where a parasite or pathogen grows up and reproduces?

question: What is the biggest myth driving the medicalisation of FGM?

question: Why does a patient with very high blood sugar (diabetes) end up with glucose in their urine?

question: What does reproductive health truly mean according to the World Health Organization (WHO)?

options.A: A woman's physical capability to carry a pregnancy to full term safely

options.C: The biological ability to conceive and bear children without medical help
options.D: A state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being in all reproductive matters

question: What does asking a patient to smile and puff out their cheeks help evaluate?

question: Which drug class must patients NEVER mix with erectile dysfunction medications like sildenafil?

question: What do we call learning to fear something simply by watching how other people react to it?

question: Which communication trick helps a nurse truly understand what a patient normally eats?

question: Which of these is NOT a typical healthcare use for a histogram?

question: What does a survivor-centric approach in nursing care prioritize above all else?

question: Which of the following is a classic example of an obstetric emergency?

question: When should a mother have her very first postnatal checkup after giving birth in a facility?

question: Why might a mother fail to feed her child recommended healthy foods even after a great health talk?

question: How does cigarette smoking negatively affect the musculoskeletal system?

question: What usually causes secondary traumatic stress in nursing?

question: A nurse is planning care for a newly admitted client with major depressive disorder. What is the best immediate action?

question: What is the primary purpose of triage in an emergency setting?

question: Why are notifiable disease registers important for public health authorities?

question: Why is it so important to involve the community in disaster risk reduction?

question: Why might an MRI or ultrasound be ordered for a patient with a rectovaginal fistula?

question: What is the primary focus of Psychological First Aid (PFA) delivered by nurses after a disaster?

question: What score on the muscle strength grading scale indicates normal strength against full resistance?

question: What is the clock-face method used for during mealtime assistance?

question: Why do social and religious pressures in many Nigerian communities often make emotional recovery harder for a PAC patient?

question: A patient says they want to save half their leftover antibiotics for a family member who might fall sick later. How should you respond?

question: Why should a nurse avoid rushing a patient during a bed-to-wheelchair transfer?

question: What is the main reason midwives and nurses use a partograph during labor?

question: What is the main job of 'tail coverage' when using a claims-made insurance policy?

question: What is the main goal of antiretroviral therapy (ART) for someone living with HIV?

question: Why are most biotechnology-derived drugs given by injection instead of as a pill?

question: Why is it best to start improvement projects on a very small scale?

question: A local health clinic invites village leaders and women's groups to help plan a new malaria campaign. Which PHC principle is this?

question: What is a major economic benefit of educating women in developing communities?

question: Which of the following is NOT a reliable way to measure the true success of a BCC program?

question: What happens if a learning activity doesn't match what you are actually supposed to learn?

question: What are social determinants of health?

question: A nurse wants to study fatigue among emergency room nurses. After defining the topic and choosing the hospital, what is the next logical step?

question: What is the term for a patient's right to make independent decisions about their own medical treatment?

question: Why are concentrated electrolytes considered 'high-alert' medications even though they aren't narcotics?

question: Why should a low protein diet never be followed without professional supervision?

question: Why do pelvic organ prolapse conditions often lead to problems with urination?

question: What usually happens when nurse managers are left out of hospital financial planning?

question: Why does chronic high blood pressure cause small arteries to permanently narrow over time?

question: What causes a high ventilation-perfusion mismatch, like when someone has a pulmonary embolism?

question: What term describes two different observers getting similar results when watching the same event?

question: Why is it important to run physical medical tests on someone presenting with severe anxiety symptoms?

question: Why is securing a patient onto a rigid spine board or basket stretcher essential during transport?

question: What is the main goal of planning a personal diet for a patient?

question: Which common virus is strongly linked to the development of cervical cancer?

question: Why is qualitative feedback just as important as hard numbers when evaluating a health project?

question: Which measure is best for protecting a DRF from internal fraud and missing stock?

question: You find an adult collapsed on the floor, gasping occasionally and not responding when you call them. What should you do first?

question: Where is the best spot to set up a temporary disaster field hospital?
